summary: Verifies an OAuth access token and returns its token details or active status. Supply the token in `access_token`; the legacy `secret` field is deprecated. Use this endpoint to check whether an access token is active and retrieve its associated client, subject, and scopes when available.

Extends the free trial period for a specific subscription item to the specified timestamp.
The subscription item must be currently in a free trial period, and the plan must support free trials.
The timestamp must be in the future and not more than 365 days from the end of the current trial period
This operation is idempotent - repeated requests with the same timestamp will not change the trial period.

Creates a price transition for the specified subscription item.
This may create an upcoming subscription item or activate immediately depending on plan and payer rules.

Applies an existing discount to a subscription item.
Manual application is an override path: self-serve distribution rules are not enforced.
At most one active discount is allowed per subscription item; applying a different
discount replaces the currently active one. Re-applying the same active discount returns a conflict.

Returns a list of all payment attempts for a specific billing statement. The payment attempts are returned sorted by creation date,
with the newest payment attempts appearing first. Pagination is supported.

Retrieves the billing subscription for the specified organization.
This includes subscription details, active plans, billing information, and payment status.
The subscription contains subscription items which represent the individual plans the organization is subscribed to.

This request returns the list of organization invitations with "pending" status.
These are the organization invitations that can still be used to join the organization, but have not been accepted by the invited user yet.
Results can be paginated using the optional `limit` and `offset` query parameters.
The organization invitations are ordered by descending creation date.
Most recent invitations will be returned first.
Any invitations created as a result of an Organization Domain are not included in the results.

Sets the given user's password as no longer compromised. The user will no longer be prompted to reset their password on their next sign-in.

If the user is in reserved-email password quarantine, the quarantine is preserved and the returned user will still have `requires_password_reset` set to `true`. Reserved-email password quarantine can only be cleared by completing a password reset or changing/removing the password.

Creates and sends organization invitations in bulk for a specified organization. Provide 1–10 invitation objects, each with `email_address` and `role`; you can set a different role and inviter for each invitation. Invitations remain pending until accepted or revoked, and `notify` controls whether an invitation email is sent.

Marks a user's password as compromised so the user is prompted to reset it at their next sign-in. Supply the `user_id` of the user whose password you want to flag. You can optionally set `revoke_all_sessions` to revoke the user's sessions as part of the operation.

Retrieves the current credit balance for the specified organization.
Credits can be applied during checkout to reduce the charge or automatically applied to upcoming recurring charges.

Increases or decreases the credit balance for the specified organization.
Each adjustment is recorded as a ledger entry. The idempotency_key parameter
ensures that duplicate requests are safely handled.

Rotates the machine's secret key.
When the secret key is rotated, make sure to update it in your machine/application.
The previous secret key will remain valid for the duration specified by the previous_token_ttl parameter.

Retrieves the billing subscription for the specified user.
This includes subscription details, active plans, billing information, and payment status.
The subscription contains subscription items which represent the individual plans the user is subscribed to.

Replaces a role in a role set with another role. This atomically removes
the source role and reassigns any members to the destination role.

Retrieves the current credit balance for the specified user.
Credits can be applied during checkout to reduce the charge or automatically applied to upcoming recurring charges

Increases or decreases the credit balance for the specified user.
Each adjustment is recorded as a ledger entry. The idempotency_key parameter
ensures that duplicate requests are safely handled.
Revokes a pending agent task. Use `agent_task_id` to identify the task whose pending status you want to revoke.

Flips the organization domain's ownership state to verified via the
manual override path, bypassing the self-serve TXT DNS challenge. The
domain row records strategy=`manual_override` and an
`organization_domain.ownership_verified` audit event is emitted with the
same strategy.

Idempotent: re-calling on an already-verified domain returns the current
ownership state without re-emitting the audit event.

Removes the active discount from a subscription item.
The discount_id must match the subscription item's currently active discount.

Update an organization membership's metadata attributes by merging existing values with the provided parameters.
Metadata values will be updated via a deep merge. Deep means that any nested JSON objects will be merged as well.
You can remove metadata keys at any level by setting their value to `null`.

Use this request to revoke a previously issued organization invitation.
Revoking an organization invitation makes it invalid; the invited user will no longer be able to join the organization with the revoked invitation.
Only organization invitations with "pending" status can be revoked.
The request accepts the `requesting_user_id` parameter to specify the user which revokes the invitation.
Only users with "admin" role can revoke invitations.
Retrieves the settings for OAuth applications for the instance (dynamic client registration, JWT access tokens, etc.).
Updates the OAuth application settings for the instance.

Updates instance authentication settings, including allowlist restrictions, the sender address for authentication emails, progressive sign-up, and test mode. Set `from_email_address` to an alphanumeric local part only; `restricted_to_allowlist` defaults to false when omitted, and test mode defaults to true for development instances.
Retrieves the organization settings of the instance

Updates the organization settings for the instance. Use the available fields to configure organization creation, membership limits, deletion, and domain enrollment; `domains_enrollment_modes` supports automatic invitations and suggestions. The response returns the updated organization settings.

Returns a list of all subscription items for the instance. The subscription items are returned sorted by creation date,
with the newest appearing first. This includes subscriptions for both users and organizations. Pagination is supported.

Change the domain of a production instance.

Changing the domain requires updating the [DNS records](https://clerk.com/docs/deployments/overview#dns-records) accordingly, deploying new [SSL certificates](https://clerk.com/docs/deployments/overview#deploy-certificates), updating your Social Connection's redirect URLs and setting the new keys in your code.

WARNING: Changing your domain will invalidate all current user sessions (i.e. users will be logged out). Also, while your application is being deployed, a small downtime is expected to occur.

Returns 403 `domain_managed_by_integration` for applications in a Vercel-managed workspace; change the domain from the Vercel integration instead.
Retrieves the per-instance SMS communication settings, including the SMS country blocklist.

Replaces the SMS country blocklist for this instance. Pass the full set of ISO 3166-1
alpha-2 country codes that should be blocked; codes that aren't recognized as SMS-tier
countries are silently dropped from the persisted list. Omitting `blocked_country_codes`
is a no-op.

Updates the restriction settings that control allowlisting, blocklisting, and email address checks for an instance. Supply the boolean settings you want to change; the response contains the resulting restriction configuration.

Creates multiple waitlist entries from email addresses in a single request. Each entry requires `email_address`; `notify` defaults to true when omitted. You can submit 1 to 50 entries per request, but duplicate email addresses within the request are not allowed, and existing waitlist entries are returned without creating new entries.

Change the domain of a production instance.

Changing the domain requires updating the [DNS records](https://clerk.com/docs/deployments/overview#dns-records) accordingly, deploying new [SSL certificates](https://clerk.com/docs/deployments/overview#deploy-certificates), updating your Social Connection's redirect URLs and setting the new keys in your code.

WARNING: Changing your domain will invalidate all current user sessions (i.e. users will be logged out). Also, while your application is being deployed, a small downtime is expected to occur.

Returns 403 `domain_managed_by_integration` for applications in a Vercel-managed workspace; change the domain from the Vercel integration instead.

The Clerk interstitial endpoint serves an html page that loads clerk.js in order to check the user's authentication state.
It is used by Clerk SDKs when the user's authentication state cannot be immediately determined.

Returns a list of all billing statements for the instance. The statements are returned sorted by creation date,
with the newest statements appearing first. Pagination is supported.

Verifies an M2M token and returns its token details when valid. Supply the token in the `token` field. A Machine Secret Key can verify a token only when it grants access to that machine, while a Clerk Secret Key can verify any token in the instance.
Generate a new URL for accessing the Svix's management dashboard for that particular instance

Retrieves the Protect settings for the instance, including rule enforcement and prerequisite check status. Use `rules_enabled` to distinguish active enforcement from shadow evaluation, where rules are scored and recorded without blocking traffic.

Updates whether Protect rules are enforced for the instance. Set `rules_enabled` to true to enforce rules or false to return to shadow evaluation, which continues scoring and recording rules without blocking traffic.

Creates multiple invitations for the supplied email addresses. Include an `email_address` in each item; set `ignore_existing` to allow an existing invitation, but you cannot invite an address associated with an existing user. Send at most 10 invitations per request, and use `notify` to control whether invitation emails are sent.

Verifies an API key using its secret. Supply the key in the `secret` field to retrieve its metadata and status. The response includes whether the key is revoked or expired and its associated subject and scopes.

Returns a list of all prices for the instance. The prices are returned sorted by amount ascending,
then by creation date descending. This includes both default and custom prices. Pagination is supported.

Creates a custom price for a billing plan. Custom prices allow you to offer different pricing
to specific customers while maintaining the same plan structure.
Verifies a client by validating the JWT supplied in the request body. Send the token for the active client to retrieve the associated client and session details.

Returns a list of all billing plans for the instance. The plans are returned sorted by creation date,
with the newest plans appearing first. This includes both free and paid plans. Pagination is supported.
Delete a Svix app and disassociate it from the current instance
Create a Svix app and associate it with the current instance

Create an agent task on behalf of a user.
The response contains a URL that, when visited, creates a session for the user.
The agent_id is stable per agent_name within an instance. The agent_task_id is unique per call.
Returns a total count of all users that match the given filtering criteria.
Removes the ban marks from multiple user accounts in one request. Supply `user_ids` with between 1 and 50 user IDs. A 200 response returns the updated user objects.
Marks multiple users as banned, which means that all their sessions are revoked and they are not allowed to sign in again.

Checks a one-time code against the verification identified by
verification_id, and returns the verification with its updated status
(`verified`, `unverified`, `expired`, or `failed`) and attempt count, so a
backend driving its own frontend can react on every attempt — an incorrect
or expired code is reported through the status, not as an error. Resubmitting
a verification whose code was already accepted is rejected with a
`verification_already_verified` error. If the code
is correct and the email address is not already verified, it is also marked
as verified as a side effect (just as it would be in a frontend verification
flow); an already verified email address is left unchanged. It never creates
a session; to sign the user in afterwards, mint a sign-in token.

Sends a one-time code to the given email address so that a backend can
verify the user controls it (for example, in a custom, backend-driven
sign-in flow). The code is tracked on its own verification; confirm it
with attempt_verification.
Returns the list of SCIM group to organization role mappings for a directory, ordered by precedence.

Creates a new SCIM group to organization role mapping for a directory.
Mappings can be created while group role mapping is disabled on the
directory, but they only take effect once it is enabled.

Replaces the entire set of SCIM group role mappings for a directory. The position of
each item in the `mappings` array determines its precedence (the first item gets
precedence 1). Passing an empty array removes all mappings. Mappings can be replaced
while group role mapping is disabled on the directory, but they only take effect once
it is enabled.

Checks a one-time code against the verification identified by
verification_id, and returns the verification with its updated status
(`verified`, `unverified`, `expired`, or `failed`) and attempt count, so a
backend driving its own frontend can react on every attempt — an incorrect
or expired code is reported through the status, not as an error. Resubmitting
a verification whose code was already accepted is rejected with a
`verification_already_verified` error. If the code for this verification
could not be sent (the SMS provider refused or failed the send after
prepare_verification had returned), the attempt is rejected with a
`verification_code_not_sent` error and no attempt is counted; call
prepare_verification again to send a new code. If too many codes have been
checked for this phone number recently, the attempt is rejected with a
`verification_code_too_many_attempts` error and no attempt is counted; the
limit is per phone number, so wait for the `Retry-After` period rather than
sending a new code. If the code
is correct and the phone number is not already verified, it is also marked
as verified as a side effect (just as it would be in a frontend verification
flow); an already verified phone number is left unchanged. It never creates
a session; to sign the user in afterwards, mint a sign-in token.

Sends a one-time code to the given phone number so that a backend can
verify the user controls it (for example, in a custom, backend-driven
sign-in flow). The code is tracked on its own verification; confirm it
with attempt_verification.
Returns a paginated list of SAML or OIDC debug test runs for an enterprise connection.
Returns a short-lived URL that starts the IdP test flow for this connection.

Rotates the OAuth application's client secret.
When the client secret is rotated, make sure to update it in authorized OAuth clients.
Revokes an admin portal link token identified by its token ID. You can include `revocation_reason` to record why the token was revoked. The response contains the token's updated revocation state.
Returns the list of directory group to organization role mappings for a directory, ordered by precedence.

Creates a new directory group to organization role mapping for a directory.
Mappings can be created while group role mapping is disabled on the
directory, but they only take effect once it is enabled.

Replaces the entire set of directory group role mappings for a directory. The position of
each item in the `mappings` array determines its precedence (the first item gets
precedence 1). Passing an empty array removes all mappings. Mappings can be replaced
while group role mapping is disabled on the directory, but they only take effect once
it is enabled.

Revoke both OAuth access token and refresh token for the associated grant for the given OAuth application.
The request may specify either token.
JWT access tokens cannot be revoked.

Generates a new API key for the directory and returns it in the `api_key` field.
This is the only way to obtain the key after creation, so make sure to update it in
your identity provider. The previous key remains valid for a short grace period before
it expires.
Retrieve a paginated list of the user's organization invitations
Retrieve a paginated list of the user's organization memberships
Returns the active biometric credentials enrolled by the user.
Cancel a specific subscription item. The subscription item can be canceled immediately or at the end of the current billing period.

Generates a new API key for the directory and returns it in the `api_key` field.
This is the only way to obtain the key after creation, so make sure to update it in
your identity provider. The previous key remains valid for a short grace period before
it expires.

This request returns the list of organization invitations.
Results can be paginated using the optional `limit` and `offset` query parameters.
You can filter them by providing the 'status' query parameter, that accepts multiple values.
The organization invitations are ordered by descending creation date.
Most recent invitations will be returned first.
Any invitations created as a result of an Organization Domain are not included in the results.

Creates a new organization invitation and sends an email to the provided `email_address` with a link to accept the invitation and join the organization.
You can specify the `role` for the invited organization member.

New organization invitations get a "pending" status until they are revoked by an organization administrator or accepted by the invitee.

The request body supports passing an optional `redirect_url` parameter.
When the invited user clicks the link to accept the invitation, they will be redirected to the URL provided.
Use this parameter to implement a custom invitation acceptance flow.

You can specify the ID of the user that will send the invitation with the `inviter_user_id` parameter.
That user must be a member with administrator privileges in the organization.
Only "admin" members can create organization invitations.

You can optionally provide public and private metadata for the organization invitation.
The public metadata are visible by both the Frontend and the Backend whereas the private ones only by the Backend.
When the organization invitation is accepted, the metadata will be transferred to the newly created organization membership.
Retrieves all user memberships for the given organization

Adds a user as a member to the given organization.
Only users in the same instance as the organization can be added as members.

This organization will be the user's [active organization] (https://clerk.com/docs/organizations/overview#active-organization)
the next time they create a session, presuming they don't explicitly set a
different organization as active before then.

Uploads an image to set or replace an OAuth application's logo. Send the request as `multipart/form-data` with the image in the `file` field; supported types are JPEG, PNG, GIF, and WebP, and the file must not exceed 10 MB. You can provide `uploader_user_id` to credit a user with the upload.
Send an invite to the email address in a waitlist entry.

Rejects a waitlist entry and returns the resulting entry. Use the `waitlist_entry_id` path parameter to identify the entry to reject. Entries locked while a batch action is processing are unavailable for other actions.

Update organization metadata attributes by merging existing values with the provided parameters.
Metadata values will be updated via a deep merge.
Deep meaning that any nested JSON objects will be merged as well.
You can remove metadata keys at any level by setting their value to `null`.

Replace an organization's metadata attributes with the provided values.
Unlike `PATCH /v1/organizations/{organization_id}/metadata` (merge semantics), this
endpoint replaces the supplied metadata fields entirely — the prior contents of each
supplied field are discarded. Fields omitted from the request body are left unchanged.
Prefer the `PATCH` endpoint for partial updates. Use `PUT` only when you explicitly
intend to overwrite a metadata field wholesale.

Lists domains associated with an organization. Filter the results by verification status or enrollment mode, and use `limit` and `offset` to control the result window. The response includes the matching domains and their total count.
Creates a new organization domain. By default the domain is verified, but can be optionally set to unverified.
Revokes a pending sign-in token. Use the `sign_in_token_id` path parameter to identify the token; a successful response returns the token with its updated status.

Removes the password credential from the given user. This is a privileged operation and does not require the user's current password. Password removal is allowed even when the user has no other sign-in method configured.

If the user does not have a password, the user is returned unchanged and no password-deletion or user-update event is emitted. By default, existing sessions remain active. Set `sign_out_of_other_sessions` to `true` to revoke sessions active when the request is processed.
Returns the active trusted devices enrolled by the user.

Check that the user's password matches the supplied input.
Useful for custom auth flows and re-verification.
Revokes a pending actor token, changing its status to revoked. Use `actor_token_id` to identify the token; the response includes its resulting status and associated actor and user details.
Retrieves the secret key for a machine. Use the `machine_id` to identify which machine's key you need.

Replaces all of the user's email addresses with a single primary email address.
By default the new email address is created verified, with the admin verification strategy.
When `identification_status` is `reserved` it is created reserved instead: unverified but usable
for sign-in and locked so no other user can claim it. When it is `unverified` the address is
neither usable for sign-in nor locked. Any existing email addresses are deleted.
If an existing email address is linked to a connected account, the request is rejected; remove
the connected account first.

**Warning:** `identification_status: unverified` can lock the user out of their account. An
unverified email address cannot be used to sign in, so if the user has no other verified or
reserved identifier, deleting their existing email addresses leaves them unable to
authenticate — and unable to verify the new address, since that requires signing in. Recovery
then requires another admin API call.
Deletes the profile image associated with a user account. Use `user_id` to identify the account whose image you want to remove. A 200 response returns the updated user object.

Sets or replaces a user's profile image. Send the image in the `file` field as multipart form data, and use `user_id` to identify the account to update. A 200 response returns the updated user object.
Retrieves a billing statement by its unique identifier. Use `statementID` to inspect the statement’s payer, current status, totals, and grouped items.

Revokes the given invitation.
Revoking an invitation will prevent the user from using the invitation link that was sent to them.
However, it doesn't prevent the user from signing up if they follow the sign up flow.
Only active (i.e. non-revoked) invitations can be revoked.

Deletes the logo associated with an organization. Use `organization_id` to identify the organization whose logo you want to remove. A 200 response returns the organization with its updated logo-related fields.

Uploads an image file as the logo for an organization. Send the request as `multipart/form-data`; files must be no larger than 10 MB and use a supported image content type. A 200 response returns the organization with its logo URL.

Replaces all of the user's phone numbers with a single primary phone number.
By default the new phone number is created verified, with the admin verification strategy.
When `identification_status` is `reserved` it is created reserved instead: unverified but usable
for sign-in and locked so no other user can claim it. When it is `unverified` the phone number is
neither usable for sign-in nor locked. The new phone number is never reserved for
second factor. Any existing phone numbers are deleted; replacing a phone number that is reserved
for second factor disables the user's MFA.

**Warning:** `identification_status: unverified` can lock the user out of their account. An
unverified phone number cannot be used to sign in, so if the user has no other verified or
reserved identifier, deleting their existing phone numbers leaves them unable to authenticate —
and unable to verify the new number, since that requires signing in. Recovery then requires
another admin API call.

Revokes a stored opaque-format M2M token. Use `m2m_token_id` to identify the token and optionally provide a `revocation_reason`. JWT-format M2M tokens are stateless and cannot be revoked; a Machine Secret Key can revoke only tokens managed by its machine, while a Clerk Secret Key can revoke any token in the instance.

Replaces a role set with another role set. This is functionally equivalent to deleting
the role set but allows for atomic replacement with migration support.
Organizations using this role set will be migrated to the destination role set.
Deletes all backup codes for a user, disabling them for future use. Supply `user_id` to identify the user whose backup codes you want to disable.

Verify that the provided TOTP or backup code is valid for the user.
Verifying a backup code will result it in being consumed (i.e. it will
become invalid).
Useful for custom auth flows and re-verification.

Refreshes a session by creating a new session token. A 401 is returned when there
are validation errors, which signals the SDKs to fall back to the handshake flow.
Revokes an API key identified by its ID. You can include `revocation_reason` to record why the key was revoked. The response contains the API key's updated revocation state.
Retrieves the secret for an API key by its identifier. Supply the key ID using the `ak_` or `api_key_` prefix followed by 32 hexadecimal characters. Treat the returned secret as a credential.

Creates a new machine scope, allowing the specified machine to access another machine.
Maximum of 150 scopes per machine.

Adds one or more roles to an existing role set.
You can optionally update the default role or creator role when adding new roles.

Sets the status of a session as "revoked", which is an unauthenticated state.
In multi-session mode, a revoked session will still be returned along with its client object, however the user will need to sign in again.

Creates a session JSON Web Token (JWT) for the specified session. You can optionally set `expires_in_seconds` to override the default token lifetime; the value must be between 30 and 315360000 seconds.

Update a user's metadata attributes by merging existing values with the provided parameters.

This endpoint behaves differently than the *Update a user* endpoint.
Metadata values will not be replaced entirely.
Instead, a deep merge will be performed.
Deep means that any nested JSON objects will be merged as well.

You can remove metadata keys at any level by setting their value to `null`.

Replace a user's metadata attributes with the provided values.

Unlike `PATCH /v1/users/{user_id}/metadata` (merge semantics), this endpoint
replaces the supplied metadata fields entirely — the prior contents of each
supplied field are discarded. Fields omitted from the request body are
left unchanged.

Prefer the `PATCH` endpoint for partial updates. Use `PUT` only when you
explicitly intend to overwrite a metadata field wholesale.
Removes the lock from a user account. Use `user_id` to identify the user whose lock you want to remove. A 200 response returns the updated user object.
Removes the ban mark from a user account. Use `user_id` to identify the user whose ban you want to remove. A 200 response returns the updated user object.

Marks the given user as locked, which means they are not allowed to sign in again until the lock expires.
Lock duration can be configured in the instance's restrictions settings.
Deletes all TOTP credentials associated with a user. Supply the `user_id` of the user whose TOTPs you want to delete; the operation removes all of that user's TOTPs.
Marks the given user as banned, which means that all their sessions are revoked and they are not allowed to sign in again.
Disable all of a user's MFA methods (e.g. OTP sent via SMS, TOTP on their authenticator app) at once.

Deletes a single SCIM group role mapping. Mappings can be deleted while group role
mapping is disabled on the directory, but the change only takes effect once it is
enabled.

Deletes a single directory group role mapping. Mappings can be deleted while group role
mapping is disabled on the directory, but the change only takes effect once it is
enabled.

Removes a permission from an organization role. Use the `organization_role_id` and `permission_id` path parameters to identify the role and permission to unlink. The response contains the updated role and its remaining permissions.

Assigns a permission to an organization role. Use the `organization_role_id` and `permission_id` path parameters to identify the role and permission to link. The response contains the updated role and its permissions.
Revokes an active biometric credential enrolled by the user.

Toggles the delivery by Clerk for a template of a given type and slug.
If disabled, Clerk will not deliver the resulting email or SMS.
The app developer will need to listen to the `email.created` or `sms.created` webhooks in order to handle delivery themselves.
Use this request to get an existing organization invitation by ID.
Removes the given membership from the organization
Updates the properties of an existing organization membership

Fetch the corresponding OAuth access token for a user that has previously authenticated with a particular OAuth provider.
For OAuth 2.0, if the access token has expired and we have a corresponding refresh token, the access token will be refreshed transparently the new one will be returned.

Retrieve a reverification scoped to a session. A resource server can use this to validate a reverification id it received from its client: confirm it is real, scoped to the expected session, completed, and how fresh each factor is. Single-use / replay detection is the caller's responsibility (the id is stable, so the caller dedups consumed ids).
Deletes an external account associated with a user. Supply the `user_id` and `external_account_id` for the account you want to remove.

Deletes a domain from an organization. Use the `organization_id` and `domain_id` path parameters to identify the organization and domain to remove. A successful response indicates that the domain was deleted.
Updates the properties of an existing organization domain.
Revokes an active trusted device enrolled by the user.
Delete the web3 wallet identification for a given user.

Returns a preview of a template using the specified template type, slug, and optional body values. Use the body fields to preview changes; `subject`, `from_email_name`, and `reply_to_email_name` apply only to email templates.
Reverts an email or SMS template to its corresponding system default. Use `template_type` and `slug` to identify the template to restore.
Deletes a machine scope, removing access from one machine to another.

Creates a JSON Web Token (JWT) for the specified session using a JWT template defined for your instance. Use `template_name` to select the template and optionally set `expires_in_seconds` to override the token lifetime, between 30 and 315360000 seconds.
Delete the passkey identification for a given user. The user is notified through email or SMS unless the passkey registration was never completed.

Returns the users who may verify an email code instead of reaching their identity provider when
enterprise SSO is unreachable.

Puts a user on the allowlist. The request is rejected unless the user holds a verified email
address on a domain one of the instance's enterprise connections serves.

Creates a single-use admin portal link token, optionally scoped to an organization and IT contact. Supply `organization_id`, `it_contact_id`, `scopes`, and `seconds_until_expiration` as needed; the expiration defaults to 3600 seconds. Treat the returned token as a secret because it is URL-borne.

This request returns the list of organization invitations for the instance.
Results can be paginated using the optional `limit` and `offset` query parameters.
You can filter them by providing the 'status' query parameter, that accepts multiple values.
You can change the order by providing the 'order' query parameter, that accepts multiple values.
You can filter by the invited user email address providing the `query` query parameter.
The organization invitations are ordered by descending creation date by default.
Retrieves all organization user memberships for the given instance.
Retrieves all organization permissions for the given instance.
Creates a new organization permission for the given instance.

Returns the list of enterprise connections for the instance.
Results can be paginated using the optional `limit` and `offset` query parameters.

Creates a new enterprise connection for an identity provider and associates it with one or more domains. Supply `name`, `provider`, and at least one valid fully qualified domain name in `domains`; choose `saml` or `oidc` settings to configure the connection for the selected provider. When `active` is true, provide IdP metadata in `saml` for SAML connections.
Get a list of all identifiers allowed to sign up to an instance
Create an identifier allowed to sign up to an instance
Get a list of all identifiers which are not allowed to access an instance
Create an identifier that is blocked from accessing an instance

Retrieves a list of all organization domains within the current instance.
This endpoint can be used to list all domains across all organizations
or filter domains by organization, verification status, enrollment mode, or search query.

The response includes pagination information and details about each domain
including its verification status, enrollment mode, and associated counts.

This request returns the list of OAuth applications for an instance.
Results can be paginated using the optional `limit` and `offset` query parameters.
The OAuth applications are ordered by descending creation date.
Most recent OAuth applications will be returned first.

Creates a new OAuth application with the given name and callback URL for an instance.
The callback URL must be a valid URL.
All URL schemes are allowed such as `http://`, `https://`, `myapp://`, etc...

This request returns the list of organization roles for the instance.
Results can be paginated using the optional `limit` and `offset` query parameters.
The organization roles are ordered by descending creation date.
Most recent roles will be returned first.

Creates a new organization role with the given name and permissions for an instance.
The key must be unique for the instance and start with the 'org:' prefix, followed by lowercase alphanumeric characters and underscores only.
You can optionally provide a description for the role and specify whether it should be included in the initial role set.
Organization roles support permissions that can be assigned to control access within the organization.

Returns the list of SAML Connections for an instance.
Results can be paginated using the optional `limit` and `offset` query parameters.
The SAML Connections are ordered by descending creation date and the most recent will be returned first.
Deprecated: Use the Enterprise Connections API instead. This endpoint will be removed in future versions.

Create a new SAML Connection.
Deprecated: Use the Enterprise Connections API instead. This endpoint will be removed in future versions.
Returns a list of all directories for the instance.

Creates a SCIM directory for the instance and associates it with an enterprise connection. Supply `enterprise_connection_id` and `provider`; you can also include group-to-role mappings to create with the directory. The created directory response includes its SCIM endpoint URL and API key.

Retrieve a list of waitlist entries for the instance.
Entries are ordered by creation date in descending order by default.
Supports filtering by email address or status and pagination with limit and offset parameters.

Creates a new waitlist entry for the given email address.
If the email address is already on the waitlist, no new entry will be created and the existing waitlist entry will be returned.

Creates a new email address for a user. Supply `user_id` and an RFC 5322-formatted `email_address`; optionally set `verified` or `primary` when creating it. If omitted, `primary` defaults to false unless this is the user's first email address.

Creates a new sign-in token and associates it with the given user.
By default, sign-in tokens expire in 30 days.
You can optionally supply a different duration in seconds using the `expires_in_seconds` property.
Creates a testing token for use with Frontend API requests. Pass the returned `token` value in the `__clerk_testing_token` query parameter; the response includes its expiration time as `expires_at`.
Lists JWT templates, with an option to return paginated or unpaginated results. Use `limit` and `offset` to control the number of templates returned and the starting position.

Creates a JWT template with the supplied name and claims. Include `name` and `claims`; set `lifetime` and `allowed_clock_skew` within their permitted ranges, and provide a signing algorithm and key when `custom_signing_key` is true. The response returns the created template.

This request returns the list of organizations for an instance.
Results can be paginated using the optional `limit` and `offset` query parameters.
The organizations are ordered by descending creation date.
Most recent organizations will be returned first.

Creates a new organization with the given name for an instance.
You can specify an optional slug for the new organization.
If provided, the organization slug can contain only lowercase alphanumeric characters (letters and digits) and the dash "-".
Organization slugs must be unique for the instance.
You can provide additional metadata for the organization and set any custom attribute you want.
Organizations support private and public metadata.
Private metadata can only be accessed from the Backend API.
Public metadata can be accessed from the Backend API, and are read-only from the Frontend API.
The `created_by` user will see this as their [active organization](https://clerk.com/docs/organizations/overview#active-organization)
the next time they create a session, presuming they don't explicitly set a different organization as active before then.

Creates a phone number for a user. Provide `user_id` and an E.164-formatted `phone_number`; set `verified` to true before reserving the number for multi-factor authentication. A 200 response returns the created phone number and its verification, linkage, and reservation details.
Lists all whitelisted redirect_urls for the instance

Creates a redirect URL. When you provide a request body, include `url` as a full URL prefixed with `https://` or a URL using a custom scheme. The response includes the created redirect URL and its timestamps.

Create an actor token that can be used to impersonate the given user.
The `actor` parameter needs to include at least a "sub" key whose value is the ID of the actor (impersonating) user.

This endpoint can be used to validate that a proxy-enabled domain is operational.
It tries to verify that the proxy URL provided in the parameters maps to a functional proxy that can reach the Clerk Frontend API.

You can use this endpoint before you set a proxy URL for a domain. This way you can ensure that switching to proxy-based
configuration will not lead to downtime for your instance.

The `proxy_url` parameter allows for testing proxy configurations for domains that don't have a proxy URL yet, or operate on
a different proxy URL than the one provided. It can also be used to re-validate a domain that is already configured to work with a proxy.
Returns a list of all directories for the instance.

Creates a directory for provisioning users from an identity provider and associates it with an enterprise connection. Supply `enterprise_connection_id` and `provider`; optionally include a name and group-to-role mappings to create with the directory. The response includes the directory configuration and its API key.
Returns all non-revoked invitations for your application, sorted by creation date

Creates a new invitation for the given email address and sends the invitation email.
Keep in mind that you cannot create an invitation if there is already one for the given email address.
Also, trying to create an invitation for an email address that already exists in your application will result to an error.

Lists stored opaque-format M2M tokens for a specific machine; stateless JWT-format tokens are not included. Use `revoked` and `expired` to filter the results, and `limit` and `offset` to control pagination. Authenticate with a Machine Secret Key to retrieve tokens for its machine, or a Clerk Secret Key to retrieve tokens for any machine in the instance.

Creates a new M2M token for the machine associated with the Machine Secret Key used to authenticate the request. Use `token_format` to choose opaque or JWT format and `seconds_until_expiration` to set the token lifetime. Set `min_remaining_ttl_seconds` to reuse an eligible existing opaque token instead of minting a new one.

Returns a list of role sets for the instance.
Results can be paginated using the optional `limit` and `offset` query parameters.
The role sets are ordered by descending creation date by default.

Creates a new role set with the given name and roles.
The key must be unique for the instance and start with the 'role_set:' prefix, followed by lowercase alphanumeric characters and underscores only.
You must provide at least one role and specify a default role key and creator role key.

Lists API keys associated with a specified subject. Use `include_invalid` to control whether invalid keys are included, and use `query` to filter the results. Use `limit` and `offset` to paginate the results.

Creates an API key for the specified subject. Supply `name` and `subject`, and provide optional claims, scopes, creator, and expiration settings as needed. The response includes the key secret, so handle it as a credential.

Retrieves the current instance configuration, including its environment, allowed origins, and subdomain access settings. Use the returned `allowed_subdomains` and `subdomain_allowlist_enabled` values to understand which subdomains may originate requests.

Updates configurable settings for an instance, including browser origins, password breach checks, and sign-in preferences. Supply only the settings you want to change; `preferred_sign_in_strategy_when_password_required` accepts `password`, `otp`, or an empty string.

This request returns the list of machines for an instance. The machines are
ordered by descending creation date (i.e. most recent machines will be
returned first)
Creates a new machine. Provide a `name` and optionally configure its machine scopes and default token TTL. The response includes the machine's secret key, so store it securely.

Returns a list of sessions matching the provided criteria.
The sessions are returned sorted by creation date, with the newest sessions appearing first.

Note: This endpoint does not return all sessions that have ever existed. Old and inactive sessions are periodically cleaned up and will not be included in the results.

**Deprecation Notice (2024-01-01):** All parameters were initially considered optional, however
moving forward at least one of `client_id` or `user_id` parameters should be provided.

Create a new active session for the provided user ID.

**This operation is intended only for use in testing, and is not available for production instances.** If you are looking to generate a user session from the backend,
we recommend using the [Sign-in Tokens](https://clerk.com/docs/reference/backend-api/tag/Sign-in-Tokens#operation/CreateSignInToken) resource instead.

Returns a list of all clients. The clients are returned sorted by creation date,
with the newest clients appearing first.
Warning: the endpoint is being deprecated and will be removed in future versions.

Use this endpoint to get a list of all domains for an instance.
The response will contain the primary domain for the instance and any satellite domains. Each domain in the response contains information about the URLs where Clerk operates and the required CNAME targets.

Add a new domain for your instance.
Useful in the case of multi-domain instances, allows adding satellite domains to an instance.
The new domain must have a `name`. The domain name can contain the port for development instances, like `localhost:3000`.
Set `is_satellite` to `true` to add a satellite domain.
To migrate a production instance from an active provider domain to its first custom primary domain,
set `is_satellite` to `false`. The custom domain becomes active and the provider domain stays attached.
Additional custom primary domains are not supported.
If you're planning to configure the new satellite domain to run behind a proxy, pass the `proxy_url` parameter accordingly.
Adding a custom primary domain returns 403 `domain_managed_by_integration` for applications in a Vercel-managed workspace; change the domain from the Vercel integration instead.

Returns a list of all users.
The users are returned sorted by creation date, with the newest users appearing first.

To walk more than a few pages, paginate with `starting_after` rather than `offset`.
A cursor page costs the same no matter how far into the list it sits, while a large `offset`
has to walk and discard every row before it, so it gets progressively slower and eventually
times out. Cursor pagination requires the `created_at` ordering, which is the default.

Creates a new user. Your user management settings determine how you should setup your user model.

By default, any email address and phone number created using this method is marked as verified. Use the `email_address_identification_status` and `phone_number_identification_status` arrays to instead create some or all of them as reserved (unverified but usable for sign-in and locked so no other user can claim them).

Note: If you are performing a migration, check out our guide on [zero downtime migrations](https://clerk.com/docs/deployments/migrate-overview).

The following rate limit rules apply to this endpoint: 1000 requests per 10 seconds for production instances and 100 requests per 10 seconds for development instances
Retrieves the instance's JSON Web Key Set. Use the returned keys when you need the public key material associated with the instance.
Removes the user from the allowlist, across every enterprise connection that serves them.

Deletes an organization permission.
System permissions cannot be deleted.
Retrieves the details of an organization permission.

Updates the properties of an existing organization permission.
System permissions cannot be updated.
Deletes the enterprise connection whose ID matches the provided `enterprise_connection_id` in the path.
Fetches the enterprise connection whose ID matches the provided `enterprise_connection_id` in the path.

Updates the enterprise connection whose ID matches the provided `enterprise_connection_id` in the path.
When enabling the connection (setting `active` to true), any existing verified organization domains that match the connection's domains (e.g. used for enrollment modes like automatic invitation) may be deleted so the connection can be enabled.
Deletes an identifier from the instance allow-list. Use the `identifier_id` path parameter to select the entry to remove. The response confirms whether the object was deleted.
Deletes an identifier from the instance block-list. Supply `identifier_id` to select the block-list identifier; a successful response indicates whether the object was deleted.

Deletes the given OAuth application.
This is not reversible.
Fetches the OAuth application whose ID matches the provided `id` in the path.

Updates an existing OAuth application with the properties you provide. Use `scopes` to replace the application's complete built-in and custom scope ceiling, rather than adding individual scopes. Include required built-in scopes and use custom scope keys from the instance OAuth scope catalog.

Deletes the organization role.
The role cannot be deleted if it is currently used as the default creator role, domain default role, assigned to any members, or exists in any invitations.
Use this request to retrieve an existing organization role by its ID.

Updates an existing organization role.
You can update the name, key, description, and permissions of the role.
All parameters are optional - you can update only the fields you want to change.
If the role is used as a creator role or domain default role, updating the key will cascade the update to the organization settings.

Deletes the SAML Connection whose ID matches the provided `id` in the path.
Deprecated: Use the Enterprise Connections API instead. This endpoint will be removed in future versions.

Fetches the SAML Connection whose ID matches the provided `saml_connection_id` in the path.
Deprecated: Use the Enterprise Connections API instead. This endpoint will be removed in future versions.

Updates the SAML Connection whose ID matches the provided `id` in the path.
Deprecated: Use the Enterprise Connections API instead. This endpoint will be removed in future versions.

Deletes a directory and stops provisioning for it. SCIM requests authenticated
with the directory's API key are rejected afterwards.
Retrieves the configuration for a SCIM directory. Use its identifier to look up details such as its provider, endpoint URL, enabled state, and attribute mappings.
Updates the configuration of a SCIM directory. Supply only the settings you want to change; `attribute_mapping` entries are merged, and setting a key to `null` removes it from the mapping.
Deletes a pending waitlist entry. Use the `waitlist_entry_id` path parameter to identify the entry to delete. Entries locked while a batch action is processing are unavailable for other actions.
Deletes an email address by its identifier. Use `email_address_id` to select the address to remove. The response confirms the deletion and identifies the deleted object.
Retrieves an email address and its verification and association details. Use `email_address_id` to identify the address to inspect.

Updates an existing email address's verification or primary status, or its notification behavior. Supply any of `verified`, `primary`, or `notify_primary_email_address_changed` to change that setting. The notification option applies when the update makes this address the user's new primary address.
Deletes a JWT template by its identifier. Use `template_id` to select the template to remove. The response indicates whether the template was deleted.
Retrieves the details of a JWT template by its identifier. Use `template_id` to select the template whose claims, lifetime, and signing configuration you need.

Updates an existing JWT template's configuration. Include `name` and `claims`; `lifetime` and `allowed_clock_skew` must fall within their permitted ranges, and custom signing details are required when `custom_signing_key` is true. The response returns the updated template.

Deletes the given organization.
Please note that deleting an organization will also delete all memberships and invitations.
This is not reversible.

After the organization is deleted, any user's active sessions that contain the deleted
organization will be cleared.
Fetches the organization whose ID or slug matches the provided `id_or_slug` URL query parameter.

Updates an existing organization.

As of API version 2026-05-12, this endpoint no longer accepts `public_metadata` or `private_metadata`.
Use `PATCH /v1/organizations/{organization_id}/metadata` to merge updates into existing metadata, or `PUT /v1/organizations/{organization_id}/metadata` to replace a metadata field entirely.
Deletes a phone number by its identifier. Use this operation to remove a phone number you no longer need; the response confirms whether it was deleted.
Retrieves the details of a phone number. Use its identifier to get the phone number, verification details, linked resources, and reservation status.

Updates verification, primary-phone, or multi-factor authentication reservation settings for a phone number. Supply only the fields you want to change; reserving the number for multi-factor authentication requires it to be verified.
Remove the selected redirect URL from the whitelist of the instance
Retrieve the details of the redirect URL with the given ID

Deletes a directory and stops provisioning for it. Provisioning requests authenticated
with the directory's API key are rejected afterwards.
Retrieves the configuration for a directory used to provision users from an identity provider. Use `directory_id` to identify the directory whose details you need.

Updates configurable properties of a directory used to provision users from an identity provider. Supply only the fields you want to change; `attribute_mapping` entries are merged into the existing mapping, and a key set to `null` is removed.

Permanently deletes the given invitation and the copies of the invitation email Clerk stored for its recipient.
Unlike revoking, deleting removes the invitation record itself, which helps honor a data erasure request from someone who was invited but never signed up.
Other records that contain the same email address, such as users or organization invitations, are not affected.
Invitations of any status can be deleted.

Returns a list of all templates.
The templates are returned sorted by position.

Retrieves a role set by its key or ID, including its roles and organization-member defaults. Use `role_set_key_or_id` to identify the role set; the response also includes its type and creation and update timestamps.

Updates an existing role set.
You can update the name, key, description, type, default role, or creator role.
All parameters are optional - you can update only the fields you want to change.
Deletes an API key identified by its ID. Supply the identifier using the `ak_` or `api_key_` prefix followed by 32 hexadecimal characters. The response confirms that the key was deleted.

Retrieves an API key by its identifier. Supply the key ID in the path using either the `ak_` or `api_key_` prefix followed by 32 hexadecimal characters. The response contains the key's configuration and status.

Updates configurable properties of an API key. Include only the fields you want to change, such as `scopes`, `description`, `subject`, or `seconds_until_expiration`. The response contains the updated API key object.
Deletes a machine. Use its `machine_id` to identify the machine you want to remove. The response confirms deletion with the machine ID and a `deleted` value.
Retrieves the details of a machine. Use its `machine_id` to identify the machine whose configuration and scopes you need to inspect.

Updates an existing machine.
Only the provided fields will be updated.

Retrieves the details and current status of a session identified by its session ID. Use `session_id` to look up the session and inspect its user, client, activity timestamps, expiry, and latest activity when available.
Retrieve the details of the sign-up with the given ID

Updates an existing sign-up with the fields you provide. Use `external_id` to associate the sign-up with an identifier from your external system, or set `custom_action` to mark it as a custom action. The response includes the sign-up's current status and verification details.
Retrieves the details of a client and its associated session information. Use `client_id` to look up the client whose sessions and authentication state you need to inspect.

Deletes a domain for the instance.
The instance's active domain cannot be deleted.
Deleting a non-satellite domain returns 403 `domain_managed_by_integration` for applications in a Vercel-managed workspace; change the domain from the Vercel integration instead.

The `proxy_url` can be updated only for production instances.
Update one of the instance's domains. Both primary and satellite domains can be updated.
If you choose to use Clerk via proxy, use this endpoint to specify the `proxy_url`.
Whenever you decide you'd rather switch to DNS setup for Clerk, simply set `proxy_url`
to `null` for the domain. When you update a production instance's primary domain name,
you have to make sure that you've completed all the necessary setup steps for DNS and
emails to work. Expect downtime otherwise. Updating a primary domain's name will also
update the instance's home origin, affecting the default application paths.
Updating the `name` or `is_secondary` of a primary domain returns 403 `domain_managed_by_integration` for applications in a Vercel-managed workspace; change the domain from the Vercel integration instead.
Deletes the specified user. Use `user_id` to identify the user to remove; the response confirms whether the deletion occurred.
Retrieves the details of a user by their identifier. Use `user_id` to select the user whose account details you need.

Update a user's attributes.

You can set the user's primary contact identifiers (email address and phone numbers) by updating the `primary_email_address_id` and `primary_phone_number_id` attributes respectively.
Both IDs should correspond to verified identifications that belong to the user.

You can remove a user's username by setting the username attribute to null or the blank string "".

As of API version 2026-05-12, this endpoint no longer accepts `public_metadata`, `private_metadata`, or `unsafe_metadata`.
Use `PATCH /v1/users/{user_id}/metadata` to merge updates into existing metadata, or `PUT /v1/users/{user_id}/metadata` to replace a metadata field entirely.
Retrieves the details of an email or SMS template by its slug. Use `template_type` to select the template category and `slug` to identify the template. This operation is deprecated.
Updates the existing template of the given type and slug
